design_intent: The leader declares and can atomically revise a mission Task graph. Task authority executes its internal control flow deterministically. It is graph engineering, not a Workflow authority or leader-driven orchestration loop.

entities.TaskGraphRevision: One immutable leader-authored definition of current Task nodes and typed control edges.
entities.Task: Stable graph node with goal criterion, Worker assignment, model alias, and identity across graph revisions. It is not one execution run.
entities.Attempt: Immutable execution history for one Task activation and its exact accepted prerequisite Attempts.
entities.OperationReceipt: Durable identity and result for exact graph or Task command replay. It is not Task state.

value_objects.ModelAlias: A configured model-selection label. It is separate from stable Worker identity and resolves when an Attempt starts.
value_objects.TaskVersionRef: Opaque concurrency coordinate for the current derived Task projection.
value_objects.GraphVersionRef: Opaque concurrency coordinate for the current complete graph revision.
value_objects.ActivationKey: Digest of current Task definition lineage, repair traversals, and accepted prerequisite Attempt IDs.

relations.goal_achieved: Forward edge from prerequisite to dependent. The complete forward subgraph is acyclic.
relations.goal_failed: Explicit bounded edge from a failed Task to itself or one earlier transitive prerequisite. It can close a directed cycle.

excluded_entities.Workflow: Task authority already owns graph revisions and deterministic control transitions.
excluded_entities.Criterion: Criterion meaning remains in Task goal prose until machines must address criteria separately.
excluded_entities.RetryTask: A new Attempt preserves stable Task identity and avoids replacement Tasks.
excluded_entities.SchedulerState: Ready, waiting, occupancy, and failure gates are derived from authority records.

limits.model_alias_capacity: one in the prototype; a later configured resolver can expose a different finite capacity

task_state_notes.dependency_waiting: Derived from current unaccepted prerequisites. It is never authored as blocked.
task_state_notes.ready: Derived when all current success prerequisites achieved their goals and one executor slot is eligible.
task_state_notes.in_progress: One exact Attempt is current and occupies its executor slot.
task_state_notes.goal_failed: The current goal cannot advance. A typed reason distinguishes criterion failure, dependency failure, and exhausted failure edge.
task_state_notes.goal_achieved: The current Attempt passed the current criterion and is the only state that satisfies a success edge.
task_state_notes.blocked: An in-progress Attempt has an external non-graph impediment with evidence. It releases its executor slot without completing.
task_state_notes.cancelled: Administrative termination. It is not goal failure and never traverses a failure edge.

transition_rules.effect: Unchanged Task definitions and current exact inputs retain accepted results. Changed or removed definitions supersede in-flight Attempts.

invariants.text: Dependency waiting is derived. A dependency_waiting Task has no block transition or blocker evidence requirement.
Attempt completion is historical fact. Only current goal_achieved satisfies a forward edge.
Every Attempt captures graph revision, Task definition lineage, Worker, model-alias resolution, and exact prerequisite Attempt IDs.
A superseded Attempt cannot become current goal_achieved or release successors.
The goal_achieved subgraph is acyclic. A goal_failed edge targets self or one transitive prerequisite and has a finite traversal bound.
Every directed cycle contains a bounded goal_failed edge. Exact traversals remain immutable Attempt provenance.
A join is ready only when all current prerequisite Attempts are goal_achieved.
A terminal failed, exhausted, or cancelled prerequisite becomes a typed dependency failure on each dependent.
Cancellation never traverses goal_failed and never erases Attempt or graph-revision history.
Exact operation replay returns the durable receipt. Changed reuse refuses before graph, Task, event, or delivery changes.
One current in_progress Attempt occupies one Worker slot. Waiting, blocked, superseded, and terminal Attempts do not.
Task authority commits control events and operation receipt before coordination publication or presentation.
A graph revision is atomic. Unchanged Task definitions retain meaning; changed definitions get a new lineage and recompute control state.
Worker identity and model alias are separate coordinates. Alias resolution is captured per Attempt, not rewritten into Task history.

graph_validation: Task keys are unique; every Task has one stable Worker assignee and one configured model alias, defaulting to default.
needs contains unique current Task keys and the complete goal_achieved subgraph has no cycle.
on_goal_failed contains one target and max_traversals from 1 through 8.
A goal_failed target is self or one transitive success prerequisite.
Graph revision uses one operation ID and the exact current GraphVersionRef.
Removing or changing a Task never deletes its prior revisions, Attempts, results, or edge traversals.
recovery_order: Fold committed graph revisions, Attempt events, failure-edge traversals, cancellations, and operation receipts.
Derive current Task definition lineage and ActivationKeys.
Derive goal_achieved inputs, dependency_waiting, goal_failed gates, and Worker occupancy.
Fence deliveries whose TaskVersionRef or ActivationKey is stale.
Persist missing ready-front delivery intent at most once per Task version.
Publish missing coordination evidence without changing Task control state.

measured_o200k_base_tokens.measurement_scope: provider name, description, and parameters; compact registration-order JSON; provider framing excluded

model_surface.replacement: Replace task_create with declarative task_graph_apply. Replace closed with goal_achieved and remove authored open/dependency states.

task_graph_apply.expected_graph_version: optional GraphVersionRef; absent only for first apply

tasks.title: string
tasks.model: optional configured alias: default or capable

routine_task_card.state: dependency_waiting, ready, in_progress, goal_failed, goal_achieved, blocked, or cancelled
routine_task_card.failure: optional typed reason and Task IDs
routine_task_card.model: configured alias; resolved model remains in Attempt trace

model_surface.full_attempt_history: Machine trace only; it is not repeated in routine model cards.
